title: Lamb Tagine with Arabian Spices
description: A fusion of Japanese and Arabian flavors, this lamb tagine is a hearty and aromatic dish. The vibrant spices and peppery notes will transport your taste buds to the Middle East.

ingredients.name: arabian spice blend
ingredients.notes: available at most Middle Eastern markets

ingredients.name: saudi saffron threads
ingredients.notes: soak in 2 tablespoons hot water before adding

ingredients.name: vibrant ras el hanout
ingredients.notes: add depth and warmth to the dish

instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the lamb pieces in batches until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes per batch.
Remove the lamb from the pot and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the chopped onion to the pot.
Cook until the onion is softened and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the Arabian spice blend, saffron threads (with their soaking liquid), and ras el hanout to the pot.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the spices are fragrant.
Add the browned lamb back to the pot, along with the sake and enough water to cover the lamb.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cover the pot and transfer it to the oven.
Bake at 300°F for 2 1/2 hours, or until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Season with green chili flakes to taste.
Serve the lamb tagine hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
